mutant.description: THE FIXTURE SET IS THE MUTANT SET, AND IT MUTATES THE INPUT RATHER THAN THE CODE -- six inputs driving one build, each of which could have collapsed into a neighbour and did not. The load-bearing one is `as_of: null` CARRYING ALL NINE VALID BOOKS: without the raise it is byte-indistinguishable from `populated`, with it byte-identical to a transport failure, so it could have failed in EITHER direction. The second is the pair (unselected, empty): the criterion is that they DIFFER, and the cheap implementation makes them identical -- so the hash compare is a test the cheap version fails. TYPECHECKER CONTROL: exercised earlier this session on this same tsc project -- a planted `const __probe: number = "not a number"` produced TS2322 rc=2 and the file was restored byte-identical (diff -q), which is what makes the rc=0 here evidence rather than a possible cached-skip on a project-references build.
mutant.expected: The assertion must FAIL against the mutated input/code and PASS against the true one. For the render set, a state that cannot be told from its neighbour by hash is an assertion that was never tested.
mutant.observed: FIRED. Six inputs against one build produced five distinct sha256; the two that could have collapsed did not. unselected c05fc9fd65e27304 != empty 6db0b0cf03b83b78 is the criterion, and the cheap implementation (folding unselected into empty) makes them identical -- so this is a test the cheap version fails. The as_of-null mutant, carrying all nine valid books, again rendered byte-identical to a transport failure rather than to populated.

determinism.method: The six captures were produced by separate invocations of the same instrument against fixed fixtures; the failed/as_of-null pair reproduced byte-identical sha256 across independent runs and the other four reproduced mutually distinct ones. The fixture-match COUNT (1 of 2 vs 2 of 2) is emitted by the instrument itself on every run, so the no-network-call evidence is reproducible rather than a one-off observation.
determinism.observed: STABLE. declared_exclusions.reason: RULED CORRECT and explicitly not to be changed (1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z, msg 12353). It refuses to guess whose data to serve when identity does not determine a firm. index.mjs was not touched, and no default was added on the client either -- the client-side default is the same defect one layer up, with the same failure mode: the viewer silently receives SOME firm's data with nothing saying which.

SAT-c-3 is explicit that this is a VISIBILITY gate, not an authorization boundary. Entitlement is server-side and already enforced -- measured 2026-08-28, a real 49financial credential got 403 artifact_forbidden on cottonwood's key with a live-bearer positive control. Nothing in the picker is load-bearing for security; it decides what to OFFER, never what to ALLOW.
